mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations. This results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% despite the tight labor market, indicating that the Fed will not feel compelled to tighten policy aggressively.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a supply-side slowdown that will crimp corporate profits and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if the slowdown occurs in a regime of already-slowing GDP growth.
failure_condition: The slowdown in industrial production is accompanied by a sharp drop in the trade-weighted dollar index, which boosts export competitiveness and offsets the negative profit impact.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and depress S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if the rate hike occurs during a period of already-slowing real GDP growth.
failure_condition: The Fed accompanies the rate hike with a dovish statement indicating that it expects to cut rates in the near future, which eases financial conditions despite the high level of the funds rate.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts signals a coming slowdown in residential investment that will depress GDP growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The drop in housing starts is accompanied by a surge in multifamily construction, which offsets the negative impact on residential investment.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating growth in nonfarm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The growth in payrolls is concentrated in low-wage sectors, which limits the boost to consumer spending and fails to drive positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the consumer price index signals a disinflationary impulse that will allow the Fed to cut interest rates and boost S&P 500 valuations, driving positive returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The drop in CPI is driven by a collapse in oil prices, which signals a negative supply shock that will ultimately depress growth and equity valuations despite the initial easing of inflation pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in real retail sales signals a surge in consumer spending that will boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if the rise occurs during a period of already-accelerating GDP growth.
failure_condition: The rise in retail sales is driven by a surge in auto sales financed by ultra-low interest rates, which signals a temporary pull-forward of demand that will reverse in subsequent months and depress equity valuations.
